facts.text: The time coordinator publishes rosgraph_msgs::msg::Clock on the absolute /clock topic with rclcpp::ClockQoS, which the source comment describes as best-effort and volatile.
The coordinator publishes fss_time_interfaces::msg::SimClockStatus on the relative fss/sim_clock_status topic with KeepLast(10) and transient-local durability.
The coordinator creates the relative fss/clock_control service of type fss_time_interfaces::srv::SimClockControl.
The clock_control callback applies request->max_real_time_factor, then request->running, and always answers success=true with message "time_coordinator updated".
set_running stores the flag, resets the regulator and real-time requests to the current simulation time and publishes the status message.
set_max_real_time_factor stores the value, resets the regulator and real-time requests, resets the regulator timer and publishes the status message.
should_advance returns false and reports RequestNotAdvanced while running_ is false.
A 200 ms wall timer calls on_clock_status_tick.
on_clock_status_tick updates the observed real-time factor, calls publish_clock_locked and publishes the status.
publish_clock fills a rosgraph_msgs::msg::Clock from the current simulation time and publishes it when publish_clock_ and clock_pub_ are set.
The fss_time README says the coordinator provides fss/clock_control to pause/resume the clock and set max_real_time_factor at runtime.
The fss_time README documents max_real_time_factor default 1.0, says 2.0 allows up to 2x and a large positive value gives the highest practical speed.
The fss_time README documents max_real_time_factor 0.0 as disabling periodic regulator requests and not as an unconstrained free-run mode.
The coordinator sets has_parent_coordinator_ when the fss_time_parent_coordinator_endpoint parameter is not empty.
receive_parent_grant sets sim_time_ns_ to a granted time newer than the current one and publishes the clock without checking running_.

With follows_real_time_ set, should_advance advances to the real-time request (capped by the regulator request below a factor of 1.0) and waits only for a participant that neither follows real time nor has a new request.
A child coordinator registers with its parent and passes its own follows_real_time setting.
time_coordinator.launch.py declares start_coordinator_ui with the default true.
time_coordinator.launch.py starts time_coordinator_ui.py when start_coordinator_ui is true.
The coordinator UI's play/pause handler calls request_control(not self.bridge.running, self.bridge.expected_rtf).

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned-response fake with placeholder clock/status replies; no clock advance, participant accounting, lock-step scheduling or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS canned-response fake (event-driven clock control, no simulator)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free event-driven transport: it answers /clock, fss/sim_clock_status and fss/clock_control with canned messages and runs no fss_time coordinator, ZeroMQ participant network, PX4 dynamics, LiDAR renderer, DDS graph or wall-clock loop
clock and status numbers are placeholders and do not advance; the fake cannot establish clock progression, observed real-time factor, participant accounting or lock-step determinism
the fake keeps publishing the same placeholder clock sample while paused, modelling the coordinator's 200 ms status tick rather than a fresh stopped-state trajectory
the clone states no numeric envelope for max_real_time_factor; resume is operator_required and no live site envelope is supplied here
the pause service always overwrites max_real_time_factor as well as running; the fake models that, and a deployment must resume with an operator-selected factor
vehicle control (MAVROS setpoints, arming, mode changes), PX4 dynamics, LiDAR point clouds and RViz visualisation are NOT COVERED by this package

the pause holds only a root coordinator: a child coordinator (fss_time_parent_coordinator_endpoint set) advances its clock on every parent GRANT without checking running, and a parent that follows real time does not wait for a child that follows real time; the fake models a root coordinator only
any client of fss/clock_control can resume the clock while the MHS latch is held; the default time_coordinator.launch.py starts the coordinator UI, whose play button sends running=true
the status publisher is KeepLast(10) transient-local, so a new subscription may first receive a stored sample from before the latest pause or resume; the fake always answers with its current state

operator_required.name: resume
operator_required.reason: the coordinator applies max_real_time_factor as the simulation-time to wall-time ratio, but the clone states no numeric minimum or maximum for the fss/clock_control request and the launch value is a configured default, not a device bound; the operator supplies the site factor envelope for resume

safe_state.description: The acknowledged fss/clock_control service is called with running=false and max_real_time_factor=0.0; in a root coordinator (no fss_time_parent_coordinator_endpoint, the launch default) should_advance then refuses to advance the shared simulation time until any client of fss/clock_control sends running=true, such as the coordinator UI's play button. A child coordinator keeps advancing its clock on every parent grant, so there the clock is not held.
